value.rationale: The result directly addresses the central systems question behind local federated steps: whether unstable local computation necessarily destabilizes the communicated iteration. On the same two-client quadratic setting used in the defining SCAFFOLD study, it proves a clean all-\(K\) safety theorem for locally stable clients and then shows that SCAFFOLD can go strictly further, stabilizing a client whose isolated local solver expands. This clarifies a concrete role of control coupling and aggregation that convergence-rate bounds alone do not expose.
